rationales: Guttation is the loss of liquid water through leaf pores, not evaporation.
Transportation is the movement of substances within a plant.
Transpiration is the loss of water from plant surfaces by evaporation.
Transduction is not the term for water loss from plant surfaces.
Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials rather than carry out aerobic respiration.
Vacuoles mainly store substances and are not the sites of aerobic respiration.
Centrioles help organize cell division and do not carry out aerobic respiration.
G-0 is a resting state and does not duplicate chromosomes.
G-1 is a growth phase before DNA replication.
G-2 is a preparation phase after DNA replication.
The S phase is when DNA is replicated and chromosomes are duplicated.
Prophase I is the longest phase of meiosis and includes several substages.
Metaphase I is shorter and involves alignment of homologous chromosome pairs.
Anaphase I involves separation of homologous chromosomes and is not the longest phase.
Telophase I is the concluding phase of the first meiotic division.
A co-factor assists an enzyme but is not the molecule on which it acts.
A product is formed by the enzyme-catalyzed reaction.
The molecule on which an enzyme acts is called its substrate.
A co-enzyme is an assisting organic molecule, not the enzyme’s target molecule.
Glucose is a product of photosynthesis, not its byproduct.
Oxygen is released as a byproduct of photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide is a raw material used in photosynthesis.
Water is a raw material in photosynthesis, not the byproduct asked for.
Lubrication helps food move smoothly but does not mean grinding it.
Mastication is the grinding and chewing of food by the teeth.
Defecation is the elimination of undigested waste.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients.
Euglena consists of a single cell, not many cells.
Euglena is a unicellular organism.
Acellular describes entities without cellular organization, unlike Euglena.
Euglena is not a group of cells living together as a colony.
Observations provide information but are not the basis from which deductions are logically drawn in this method.
Deductions are logical consequences drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a broad, well-supported explanation rather than the immediate source of these deductions.
A law describes a consistent natural relationship and is not the source of the deductions in this context.
Primates is an order of mammals, not of the pea plant.
Pisum is the genus name of the pea plant.
Plantae is a kingdom, not an order.
Fabales is the order to which the pea plant belongs.
An organelle is a structure within a cell, not a group of similar cells.
A tissue is a group of similar cells organized to perform a function.
An organ is made of different tissues working together.
An organ system is a group of organs working together.
Experiments test a hypothesis and its predicted consequences.
Observations are recorded evidence, not the logical consequences of a hypothesis.
Deductions are the logical consequences drawn from a hypothesis.
Data are information collected, often through observations or experiments.
In the five-kingdom classification used in this context, many algae are placed in Protista.
Fungi includes organisms such as yeasts and mushrooms, not algae in this classification.
Plantae includes plants, but the textbook classification places algae in Protista.
Animalia contains animals and does not include algae.
The matrix is the fluid-filled interior of a mitochondrion, not its inner-membrane folds.
A granum is a stack of thylakoids in a chloroplast.
Cristae are the infoldings of the mitochondrial inner membrane.
A thylakoid is a membrane sac in a chloroplast.
An adult human liver normally weighs far less than 2.5 kg.
An adult human liver weighs approximately 1.5 kg.
A weight of 0.5 kg is too low for a normal adult liver.
A weight of 5 kg is far above the normal adult liver weight.
